newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand raises capital adequacy rules for banks.
newsitem.headline: Thailand raises capital adequacy rules for banks.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand on Wednesday raised capital adequacy requirements for banks and finance companies, saying the decision would put their strengthened positions in line with international standards.

The central bank also said it downgraded funds raised by banks and finance firms through floating of preferential shares with deferred dividend conditions to second-tier assets from currently classified first-tier capitals.

The central bank said the capital adequacy standard of finance companies, based on the ratio of disbursed capitals to assets, would be raised to at least 7.5 percent from January 1, 1997, and further to 8.0 percent the next year, from the current 7.0 percent.
It said the adjusted 8.0 percent capital ratio from January 1, 1998, would include a minimum 5.5 percent first-tier capital, against 5.0 percent now.
The central bank did not say by how much it was raising the capital adequacy requirements for banks.
It said funds or foreign exchange invested abroad by finance companies seeking to launch foreign exchange services would be classified as their risk assets. It did not elaborate.

Market analysts said the central bank's measures were designed to strengthen Thai banks and finance companies in the wake of their increased foreign debt exposure arising from a recent practice by these institutions to tap cheaper short-term funds abroad.
